course_name_original: Elasticidad y resistencia de materiales II
course_name_en: Elasticity and Strength of Materials II
prerequisites: Having passed previous courses, especially the 'Elasticity and Strength of Materials' course from the second year.

learning_outcomes.text: That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Knowledge and skills for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Knowledge and skills to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and skills for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Knowledge and skills for the design, analysis and calculation of mechanisms and mechanical systems.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: Block A: Advanced Concepts of Elasticity
TEMA I.- Advanced Aspects of Stresses and Deformations
Octahedral Stresses. Spherical and Deviatoric Tensor
General Components of the Displacement Field. Geometric Interpretation
TEMA II.- General Approach to the Elastic Problem
Formulation of the elastic problem in displacements. Navier's Equations
Formulation of the elastic problem in stresses. Beltrami-Michel Equations
Uniqueness of the solution to the elastic problem
Influence of Temperature. The Thermoelastic Problem
TEMA III.- Energy Theorems of Elasticity
TEMA IV.- Two-dimensional Elasticity in Cartesian Coordinates
Bending of a cantilever beam loaded at its end
Block B: Advanced Concepts of Strength of Materials
Degree of Hyperstaticity of a System
Method based on the Principle of Virtual Work
Method based on the application of Castigliano's Theorem
TEMA VI: Advanced Topics in Bending
Buckling of rings, arches and curved bars
Pure Torsion. Torsion in circular section prisms
Expression of the internal potential associated with torsion
Block C: Current Regulations: Structural Code
Checks on the element. ULS and SLS
Resistance of Sections and Section Terms
Resistance of Sections to Shear Force
Tema XII.- Serviceability Limit States and Fatigue
teaching_methods: Small group classes (problem solving, presentations, practical activities)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Written exam)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises

assessment_rules: In the theoretical exam, it is necessary to score above zero in both theoretical content (30%) and operational content (70%). The average evaluation of practice reports must be 5 or higher to be considered approved. To pass the course, both the theoretical exam and the individual work (practices) must be passed independently. Failure to pass or submit the proposed practices will prevent approval in the Ordinary Call, requiring an extraordinary exam after submission of solved practices.
